source.title: dilemmas and outcomes.pdf
source.changes: Mechanically extracted; headings and table labels omitted; whitespace joined.

Ladder.text: It is 1987 and you are on a ferry from Belgium to England. Suddenly, the ferry starts tilting and water begins to pour in. You and some other passengers are trying to get to the deck by a rope ladder. You climb up the ladder and stand on the deck, looking at the other passengers making their way up behind you. Directly below you, a man who is midway up the ladder seems frozen into immobility by fear or cold and is blocking the way. You try to speak and reach to him, but he does not react. People behind you are jostling. The ship seems to be sinking fast and the man is still blocking the ladder. From the crowd below, someone shouts that you should push the man off. If you push the man off the ladder, he will probably die, but the other people will be able to climb on deck. If you do not push the man off the ladder, he will probably continue blocking the way so that many of the people behind you will not be able to get on deck and therefore will drown. Do you push the man off the ladder?

Yes.success: You push the man off the ladder. He falls off the boat and you hear a loud splash as he enters the water. The people behind you start to climb on deck. In the end, your decision saves all of the remaining passengers - but the man dies in the process.
Yes.failure: You push the man off the ladder. However, his foot catches onto the ladder and as he falls, the ladder also falls down with him. You hear a loud splash as the man and ladder enter the water. Without the ladder, the remaining passengers have no way of making their way up to the deck. In the end, your decision does not save anyone: you watch as the man and all of the remaining passengers die.

No.success: You do not push the man off the ladder. Shortly after, he attempts to move, but is not physically able so he stumbles and falls off. You hear a loud splash as he enters the water. The people behind you start to climb on deck. In the end, your decision saves all of the remaining passengers - but the man dies in the process.
No.failure: You do not push the man off the ladder. He remains frozen and continues to block the way for all the other passengers. In the end, your decision does not save anyone: you watch as the man and all of the remaining passengers die.

Tyran.text: You are an army officer in the Dominican Republic in 1961. For decades now, your country has been governed by a dictator who has had thousands of people killed because of their ethnicity or their political views. You are a member of a group that wants a new start for your country without a civil war. To achieve this goal, you consider it unavoidable to kill the dictator in order to disempower him, his family, and his followers. For this, you and six co-conspirators are asked to ambush and kill the dictator. If you kill the dictator, the people in your country will have a chance for a new start. If you do not kill him, the regime will continue its killings. Do you kill the dictator?

Yes.success: You ambush and kill the dictator. He is successfully disempowered; most of his supporters flee the country and no longer pose a threat. In the end, your decision provides a better future for the people in your country - but the dictator dies in the process.
Yes.failure: You ambush and kill the dictator. However, his followers are prepared for war; they do not know who conspired to kill the dictator but begin to attack everyone who opposes them. In the end, your decision does not save anyone: you watch as your country’s people engage in civil war and many are injured or die in the process.

No.success: You do not kill the dictator. Shortly after, you receive news that he is killed by one of his generals in an internal power dispute. The general is arrested and most of the dictator’s supporters flee the country and no longer pose a threat. In the end, your decision provides a better future for the people in your country - but the dictator dies in the process.
No.failure: You do not kill the dictator. He continues his violent and malevolent regime. As time goes on, your country’s people become more enraged and begin to revolt. In the end, your decision does not save anyone: you watch as your country’s people engage in civil war and many are injured or die in the process.

Lifeboat.text: It is 1841, and you are the captain of a ship. After colliding with an iceberg, the ship sank. You, some other crew members, and passengers were able to save yourselves onto two lifeboats. The next day, it starts to rain. You navigate while the others scoop out the water and oar. Someone from the other lifeboat calls to you, and you say that they are overcrowded with 41 people. The large waves could make their lifeboat sink at any time and the passengers ask you what to do as you are the highest ranking officer. You think that approximately ten adults would have to leave the boat to substantially increase the chance that the other passengers will survive. However, your lifeboat is already at full capacity and you cannot accept any more passengers. The 10 passengers would have to go overboard, and you know that the water is so cold that they would freeze to death. If you tell them not to throw anybody overboard, the boat will most likely sink at some point within the next few days and all 41 people will die. If you instead tell them to throw 10 people overboard, the rest of the passengers will be able to keep rowing towards land and will have a good chance of being rescued. Do you ask them to throw 10 people overboard?

Yes.success: You tell the passengers to throw 10 people overboard. They do as you instruct, and you watch as 10 randomly selected people are tossed into the water, where they will freeze and die. The lifeboat becomes considerably lighter and there is now also more food and water available to better sustain the rest of the passengers. The rest of the passengers continue to row and a few days later, the two lifeboats reach land. In the end, your decision saves the rest of the passengers - but 10 people die in the process.
Yes.failure: You tell the passengers to throw 10 people overboard. They do as you instruct and you watch as 10 randomly selected people are tossed into the water, where they will freeze and die. The rest of the passengers continue to row but it is obvious that they are distressed by what they did. A few days pass and the passengers still have low morale. When a strong wind rocks the boat, they are afraid that more people will be thrown overboard and start fighting amongst themselves, causing the boat to topple over. In the end, your decision does not save anyone: you watch as the lifeboat sinks and all the passengers die.

No.success: You tell the passengers not to throw 10 people overboard. They do as you instruct and continue to row. A few days later, 10 passengers become dehydrated or weakened from drinking seawater and end up dying. The rest of the passengers throw the bodies overboard and continue to row. Soon after, the two lifeboats reach land. In the end, your decision saves the rest of the passengers - but 10 people die in the process.
No.failure: You tell the passengers not to throw 10 people overboard. They do as you instruct and try to scoop as much water as possible while continuing to row. A few days pass and the passengers become tired and dehydrated - partially because there is not enough food and water for everyone. Another storm comes and they cannot defend themselves because the lifeboat is overpopulated and they are also too weak. In the end, your decision does not save anyone: you watch as the lifeboat sinks and all the passengers die.

Suicide.text: You are a member of the Canadian Senate and have to vote on a new law. Canada’s health care expenses are increasing steadily, mainly because the ratio of old people increases. Recent studies indicate that the legalization of medically assisted suicide would strongly decrease medical expenses. The state considers legalizing medically assisted suicide for the patients who are terminally ill and whose life expectancy is 6 months or less. If they wish, these patients could then choose to be killed by a doctor with an overdose of tranquillizers. Experts estimate that the new law would save 139 million dollars. This money could be used for other medical treatments. If you allow medically assisted suicide, many more people will get better medical treatment improving their quality of life and life expectancy. However, you would legalize a form of killing. If you do not allow medically assisted suicide, the healthcare system will have to keep on saving money in every possible way. Do you change the law and make medically assisted suicide legal?

Yes.success: You change the law and make medically assisted suicide legal. Patients who are terminally ill and wish to die are killed. The money saved on these patients is used to help other people in need of healthcare. In the end, your actions saved some people - but you also legalized a form of killing.
Yes.failure: You change the law and make medically assisted suicide legal. However, terminally ill patients rarely take up this option as they are afraid of the additional suffering that the medically assisted suicide may induce. As a result, the healthcare system does not get additional funding, and not enough money is available for other patients. In the end, you legalized a form of killing, and your actions do not save any funds and many patients die due to low healthcare funding.

No.success: You do not change the law and medically assisted suicide remains illegal. Terminally ill patients are given the same level of care as before to maintain quality of life in their final months. The healthcare system does not get additional money, and as a result, some patients with rare diseases do not get the best treatment. In the end, your actions saved some people - but the quality of care for a small number of other patients was reduced due to lack of funding.
No.failure: You do not change the law and medically assisted suicide remains illegal. Much of the government funds is expended on maintaining quality of life for terminally ill patients in their final months. As a result, the healthcare system does not get additional funding, and not enough money is available for other patients. In the end, your actions do not save any funds and many patients die due to low healthcare funding.

Medicine.text: You are the Belgian minister of health. A 7-year-old boy who suffers from a very rare immunological disease asks you for a refund for his medicine. Without taking this medicine regularly, the boy will die. Currently, the medicine is not covered by the health care system, and it is so expensive that the family, who has been buying the medicine for years, will not be able to raise enough money for much longer (approximately 200,000 euros per year). Thus, the boy will die if you refuse the refund. If you refuse to pay for the medicine, the boy will probably die within the next few years. However, if you pay, this money will have to be saved elsewhere; thus, the quality of care for other patients would be reduced, increasing the risk that their treatments will be less effective. An independent agency estimated that funding the boy will therefore likely lead to the death of more people. Do you refund the boy’s medicine?

Yes.success: You refund the boy’s medicine. He and his family are grateful because this will be able to save his life. However, the reallocation of money leads to reduced quality of care for other patients. In the end, your decision saves the boy’s life - at the cost of reducing care for a small number of other patients.
Yes.failure: You refund the boy’s medicine. He and his family are grateful, but the treatment is unsuccessful and the boy dies. Because you had funded the boy, the reallocation of money leads to reduced quality of care for other patients, and an elderly man also dies as a result. In the end, your decision does not save anyone: the boy dies, and the lack of funds leads to the death of an elderly man.

No.success: You do not refund the boy’s medicine. The boy’s family have no choice but to seek medical help in another country. While treatment is cheaper there, it is less effective. As a result, although the boy’s illness is under control, the new medication has some minor side effects that affect his quality of life. In the end, your decision saves the boy’s life - but at some cost of minor side effects.
No.failure: You do not refund the boy’s medicine. His family can no longer afford the treatment and the boy dies. Some other patients with the same immunological disease learn of this and protest your decision outside the hospital alongside the boy’s family. An elderly patient has a heart attack during the protest and dies. In the end, your decision does not save anyone: the boy dies, and the outrage over your actions leads to the death of an elderly man.

RAF.text: You are the German head of state in 1977 and a far-left terrorist group kidnapped the President of the Federation of the German Employers’ Association. In exchange for his life, the terrorist group demands the release of 11 imprisoned members. A few years ago, the terrorist group had successfully obtained the release of 5 members by another kidnapping. 4 of the released members have since then committed further terrorist attacks that killed several innocent people. If you consent to the terrorist group’s demands, 11 former terrorists will be released and will likely commit further terrorist attacks killing several people. If you refuse, the hostage will be killed. Do you release the former terrorists?

Yes.success: You release the 11 former terrorists. The hostage is saved and returns home to his family. None of the released terrorists kills anyone, but one of them commits an attack in which an innocent civilian is severely injured. In the end, your decision saves the hostage’s life - but an innocent person is injured in the process.
Yes.failure: You release the 11 former terrorists. The hostage is saved and returns home to his family, but disappears again a few days later. Upon investigation, he is suspected to have been ambushed and killed by the terrorist group. One of the terrorists commits an attack in which an innocent civilian is severely injured. In the end, your decision does not save anyone: the hostage dies, and the terrorist attack leads to the injury of an innocent person.

No.success: You do not release the 11 former terrorists. Armed police manage to locate the hostage and orchestrate a rescue mission. The hostage is saved, but an innocent civilian is severely injured in the conflict. In the end, your decision saves the hostage’s life - but an innocent person is injured in the process.
No.failure: You do not release the 11 former terrorists. The terrorist group kills the hostage and orchestrates an attack on his family members, and one person is severely injured. In the end, your decision does not save anyone: the hostage dies, and the terrorist attack leads to the injury of an innocent person.

Rwanda.text: You are a project leader in a development aid team in Rwanda. All over the country, members of the ethnic group of Hutu attack members of the Tutsi group. The family of one of your Tutsi employees is hiding in your agency’s center. Another employee arrives and tells you that he just witnessed his whole family and another of your employees being killed by an armed group simply for being Tutsis. Shortly afterward, a crowd of armed people gathers at the center. The leader threatens to attack the building and kill all the Tutsi citizens inside unless you hand over your employee who just arrived. If you protect your employee, the mob will probably attack the center and kill many people. If you let the mob take your employee, he will be killed but the other people under your care will be safe. Do you protect your employee?

Yes.success: You protect your employee. The Hutu mob sees that your center is protected by armed security guards. The mob try to attack, injuring one guard, but flee when the other guards start to attack them back. In the end, your actions save your employee and the people in the center - but a security guard is injured in the process.
Yes.failure: You protect your employee. He stays in the building and is looking through the window when the Hutu leader shoots and kills him. Soon after, the Hutu mob attacks everyone in the center. In the end, your actions lead to the death of the employee as well as many people in the center.

No.success: You let the mob take your employee. The Hutu do not kill the man but beat him, causing some injuries to his body. They leave soon afterwards without harming anybody else. In the end, your actions save your employee’s life and the people in the center- but your employee is injured in the process.
No.failure: You let the mob take your employee. The Hutu leader kills him. However, they still decide to attack everyone in the center afterwards, resulting in many civilian deaths. In the end, your actions lead to the death of the employee as well as many people in the center.

Ransom.text: You are the German head of state and 10 of your citizens are taken hostage in the Sahara Desert by a group of terrorists. You have to decide whether to pay a ransom of several million euros. Other measures to free the hostages have been tried but did not succeed; by now, it has been going on for half a year and one woman has died. Similar situations in the past have shown that terrorists use the money to buy weapons and kill even more people. Furthermore, future tourists will more likely be kidnapped if you pay. If you pay the ransom, you can save the hostages. If you do not pay, the 10 hostages will be killed, but you will prevent future terrorism being financed, which will probably save more than 10 lives. Do you pay the ransom?

Yes.success: You pay the ransom to the terrorists. The terrorists free the hostages and they return back to Germany. However, the terrorists use the money to buy additional weapons and orchestrate an attack in which one person gets injured. In the end, your actions saved the lives of the 10 hostages - but one person was injured as a result of a terrorist attack.
Yes.failure: You pay the ransom to the terrorists. However, now that the terrorists have the money, they see no reason to free the hostages and kill them. In the end, your actions lead to the deaths of all the hostages, and the terrorists now have resources for future attacks.

No.success: You do not pay the ransom to the terrorists. Soon after, armed police find the location of the prisoners and orchestrate a plan to free them. However, one innocent civilian is injured in the conflict between the police and the terrorists. In the end, your actions saved the lives of the 10 hostages - but one person was injured in the process.
No.failure: You do not pay the ransom to the terrorists. The terrorists kill the hostages. The leader of a more prominent terrorist group hears of this and decides to join forces with them, ensuring that they have funds for future attacks. In the end, your actions lead to the deaths of all the hostages, and the terrorists now have resources for future attacks.

Tax.text: You are the state minister of finance of a German federal state. You have to decide whether or not to buy data that was obtained illegally. You have been given an offer to buy data about tax evaders. The data was compiled by hackers who have illegally invaded the servers of several foreign banks, where some of your wealthy citizens transfer their money to evade taxes. The data is probably reliable and consists of up to 50,000 transactions. If you buy the data, you will use illegally obtained information and reward hackers for data theft, which might promote cybercrime in the future - but you will be able to prosecute tax evaders, whose fines will amount to millions. If you do not buy the data, you will miss out on millions of euros of additional tax payments and fines. Do you buy the data?

Yes.success: You buy the data. This helps you find billions of evaded tax dollars. The additional money is used to pay for essential services such as healthcare, saving the lives of many citizens. However, it becomes known you colluded with criminals which consequently encouraged illegal data theft. In the end, many lives are saved as a consequence of your actions - but rumours that the government condones illegal activities might promote cybercrime.
Yes.failure: You buy the data. However, it turns out the data is not very useful, and you only catch a few minor tax evaders. As a result, you wasted a lot of government money on the purchase which could have been used to fund other essential services such as healthcare. In the end, your actions cause many people who need medical help to be negatively affected.

No.success: You do not buy the data. Since the criminals cannot get money from you, they decide instead to release the data voluntarily and set up a fundraiser to support their work as modern “Robin Hoods”. The data helps you find billions of evaded tax dollars. The additional money is used to pay for essential services such as healthcare, saving the lives of many citizens. However, the praise for the criminals by the general population also encourages illegal data theft. In the end, many lives are saved as a consequence of your actions - but praise for the criminals might promote cybercrime.
No.failure: You do not buy the data. Many more people start evading taxes as they realise there is a low probability of getting caught. This reduces government funding for essential services such as healthcare. In the end, your actions cause many people who need medical help to be negatively affected.

Operations.text: You are a physician in a hospital in a town in a rural area. Your hospital needs to perform at least 50 lung surgeries per year in order to have them refunded by health insurance. Until this December, the hospital has only conducted 48 surgeries; thus, maybe none of the surgeries will be covered by insurance. The clinic has already been in debt the previous year and will have to file for bankruptcy if there will be another debt when the knee surgeries are not refunded. Without this hospital, the region will not have access to fast intensive emergency care. Sooner or later, having no fast access to intensive emergency care will lead to avoidable deaths in the region. The only way of sustaining the clinic would be by performing two lung surgeries that are medically not indicated. If you perform two unnecessary surgeries, you can save the hospital from bankruptcy and the region will continue to have fast emergency care, but you will perform surgery on two patients for whom other treatments would be more appropriate. If you do not perform the surgeries, the clinic will be closed leading to deaths sooner or later. Do you perform the two surgeries that are not medically indicated?

Yes.success: You perform the two lung surgeries. This ensures that the hospital will receive money again and the region retains fast emergency health care. However, one of the patients has a job that pays by the hour, and taking two weeks off to recover from the unnecessary surgery causes him to lose some income. In the end, your actions sustain fast emergency healthcare for the region - but causes a patient to lose some income in the process.
Yes.failure: You perform the two lung surgeries. However, one of the surgeries causes side effects for the patient and he sues the hospital. Upon investigation, regulators discover that your hospital conducted surgeries that were medically not indicated and shut down the hospital. In the end, your actions lead to medical complications for one of the patients, and your region loses access to fast emergency care.

No.success: You do not perform the two lung surgeries. When the hospital is about to be shut down, the Ministry of Health provides additional funds to keep the hospital running. However, this funding is less than what you would have otherwise received from the insurance, resulting in reduced quality of care. In the end, your actions sustain fast emergency healthcare for the region - but the quality of care is reduced.
No.failure: You do not perform the two lung surgeries. You try to apply for additional funds for the hospital, but the application is rejected. Consequently, the lack of funding causes reduced quality of care and one patient experiences medical complications as a result. Soon after, the hospital shuts down due to lack of funding. In the end, your actions lead to medical complications for one of the patients, and your region loses access to fast emergency care.

Vet.text: You are a European veterinarian conducting animal experiments on highly contagious germs. On a daily basis, you cause suffering to animals by infecting them with deadly diseases. You are aware that this work provides important insights that, in the long run, can save many other animals. Furthermore, you are a specialist and because of your expertise you can achieve more than other veterinarians. However, you have become a vet in order to heal animals and you are considering quitting your job. If you quit your job, fewer animals will die in the lab, but there will also be fewer findings about animal diseases. As a result, the development of medicines for healing sick animals will be delayed, leading to many preventable deaths. If you continue your job of infecting animals with diseases for medical research, you will keep causing animal suffering, but your research will probably save the lives of even more animals in the future. Do you quit your job?

Yes.success: You quit your job as a veterinarian. As a result, your lab closes down and this research is discontinued, and any animals you had kept for testing were euthanized. A few years later, you come across a report which shows that most research in this area is basically worthless and many basic results could not be reproduced. You realise that while you had inflicted some suffering on animals, many lives were spared because your research was discontinued. In the end, your decision saves the lives of animals who would have potentially suffered and died - but you harmed some animals in the process.
Yes.failure: You quit your job as a veterinarian. After you close down your lab, another lab starts redoing the extensive vaccine tests you had been working on. A few years later, they publish a report showing that the vaccine you had been working on was unsafe. You realise that you would have discovered this much sooner if you had kept working in the lab. This would have prevented many animals from suffering in the study conducted by the other lab. In the end, your actions caused many more animals to suffer and die.

No.success: You continue working as a veterinarian. A few weeks later, you make an important breakthrough and successfully launch a new animal vaccine. This can save the lives of many animals, even though some animals suffered in the experimentation process. In the end, your decision saves the lives of animals who would have potentially suffered and died - but you harmed some animals in the process.
No.failure: You continue working as a veterinarian. A few years later, you come across a report which shows that most research in this area is basically worthless and its results cannot be reproduced. You realise that you had inflicted pointless suffering on those animals with little to no benefit. In the end, your actions caused many more animals to suffer and die.

Endow.text: After a long-term imprisonment, a convicted child kidnapper and murderer wants to organise a foundation for young victims of crime. You are the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate of 25,000 euros to the foundation. However, the foundation would be named after the offender, and it is unclear whether he is acting out of remorse or simply to clear his name. The family of his victim opposes such a foundation and considers it immoral, derogatory, and an exploitation of the victim. If you oppose the foundation, the money will be lost. If you approve the foundation, crime victims will benefit from the 25,000 euros and additional fund raising. Do you approve the foundation?

Yes.success: You accept the money to start the foundation. However, the parents of the victim strongly disapprove of your choice. In the end, your action helps many young victims of crime through the foundation - but you angered the family of the victim in the process.
Yes.failure: You accept the money to start the foundation. The parents of the victim are outraged and disapprove of your choice, which leads to people boycotting the foundation. News of this tarnishes the reputation of other foundations for victims of crime, as people no longer trust that they are funded by impartial individuals. Young people who are repeat victims of crime are therefore less likely to seek help as they do not trust these foundations. In the end, your actions caused outrage and more young people are victims of crime because they do not have the help that they need.

No.success: You decline the money to start the foundation. When you tell the man about your decision, it becomes apparent that he feels deep remorse about his actions; however, it is too late to change your mind as you already announced your decision in the media. An anonymous viewer sees your announcement and, because they were once a young victim of crime, offers you the same seed capital for the foundation. You start the foundation with this donation, but you regret that you did not help the man atone for his crimes. In the end, many young victims of crime are helped through your actions - but you prevented a man from atoning for his crimes and attempting to make amends.
No.failure: You decline the money to start the foundation. When you tell the man about your decision, it becomes apparent that he feels deep remorse about his actions; however, it is too late to change your mind as you already announced your decision in the media. Later, you hear of cases of young people becoming repeat victims of crime as they did not have access to adequate help. In the end, your actions prevented a man from atoning for his crimes and attempting to make amends, and more young people are victims of crime because they do not have the help that they need.

RobinHood.text: You are an employee of a bank in Germany. You have many loyal customers who trust you and your bank. Among them are some customers who are in debt and do not fulfill the conditions for being granted a loan. Interviews with them are very stressful for you and for the customers. Currently, there is one very severe case where a customer and his family would be ruined without a loan. You see an undetectable way to temporarily redirect some deposits and investments from other customers to his bank account, which would improve his credit rating sufficiently. This way you could help him as well as other customers in difficulties. At the same time, you would abuse the trust of the wealthy customers and of your superiors and commit fraud. If you temporarily redirect a part of the wealthy customers’ money, you will be able to help indebted customers but abuse trust. If you follow the rules, your indebted customers and their families will go bankrupt. Do you redirect money from wealthy customers?

Yes.success: You redirect money from wealthy customers. The customer is extremely grateful to get the loan. They use the money to buy essential supplies for their family, including a used car that is necessary for them to commute to work. This helps them find a new job, which allows them to pay back the loan. In the end, your decision saves the customer’s family - but you breach the trust of the bank and the wealthy customers by redirecting customer funds.
Yes.failure: You redirect money from wealthy customers. The customer gets the loan but invests the money poorly, and soon becomes unable to pay back the debt. Your fraud comes to light and the bank loan system gets shut down by management for investigation. As a consequence, many other poor families cannot get a loan. In the end, the customer cannot get back on his feet. Your actions breach the trust of the bank and the wealthy customers, and also leave many more people without essential bank loans.

No.success: You do not redirect money from wealthy customers. You recommend that the customer in need of a loan switch to another bank, which is more lenient but gives loans at worse conditions. The family can use this money to get back on their feet, but the bad interest rates on the loan mean that they must pay off the debt for a few years longer than if you had given them the loan. In the end, your decision does not breach the trust of anyone and saves the integrity of the bank - but the customer’s family will struggle with higher interest rates on their debt payments.
No.failure: You do not redirect money from wealthy customers. The customer cannot get a loan and the family goes bankrupt. Other poor families hear about this and become disillusioned by the bank loan system, and do not apply for loans in fear of humiliation. In the end, you do not breach the trust of anyone, but the customer cannot get back on his feet and your actions leave many more people without essential bank loans.
